title: Interagency working and integrated care
blurb: Know who does what in the MDT and across agencies, how integrated care systems work in England, and how to join up care for people.
question: A nurse is asked which organisation in an integrated care system plans local NHS services and holds the NHS budget for its population. What is the correct answer?

teach.body: Integrated care means the NHS, local councils, the voluntary sector and others working together so people get joined-up support in the right place at the right time. People are living longer with more complex conditions, and housing, income, employment and environment affect health as much as healthcare does. In plain English: no single service can meet complex needs alone, so services plan and deliver care together around the person (proficiency P7.1, P7.6).

teach.caption: Proficiency P5.4: know the roles and scope of practice of team members so referrals are timely (Code 13.2).

teach.body: Interagency working depends on sharing the right information with the right people. Caldicott principle 7 says the duty to share information for individual care is as important as the duty to protect confidentiality. Explain to the person what will be shared and why, and seek their agreement where appropriate. Code 8.3 asks nurses to keep colleagues informed when sharing care, and 8.6 to share information to identify and reduce risk.

Most errors happen at the joins: admission, transfer and discharge. Medicines lists differ, test results go unseen and plans are lost. Proficiency P7.6 asks nurses to understand these complexities. Practical safeguards include structured handover, medicines reconciliation with the prescriber or pharmacist, a named contact, and sharing the care plan with the receiving team.

teach.h: Evaluating people's experience of complex care
teach.body: Proficiency P7.7 asks nurses to monitor and evaluate the quality of people's experience of complex care. The best evidence comes from people and families themselves: ask about the whole journey across services, including the transitions, and feed what you learn into improvement.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Ward Nurse Gita and Mr Doyle
teach.body: Mr Doyle, 58, has COPD, drinks heavily and has nowhere stable to live. Gita asks for his agreement to involve the hospital alcohol liaison team, the housing team and a social worker, and requests a pharmacist review of his inhalers. She invites the community respiratory nurse to the discharge meeting and sends the plan to his GP. Each agency knows its role and Mr Doyle has one named contact.

teach.text: ICB versus ICP: the integrated care BOARD is the NHS body that plans services and holds the NHS budget. The integrated care PARTNERSHIP is the joint committee with local authorities that writes the integrated care strategy.

items: 36 ICSs in England, legally established 1 July 2022.
ICB: NHS body, plans services, manages NHS budget. ICP: joint committee, integrated care strategy.
Upper-tier local authorities are responsible for social care and public health.
Know MDT roles to refer promptly; share information for care (Caldicott 7).
Make transitions safe and ask people about their whole journey (P7.6, P7.7).

summary: You can now describe how integrated care systems, boards and partnerships work in England, the roles of members of the multidisciplinary team and partner agencies, and how to share information and coordinate care safely across settings. You can also evaluate people's experience of complex care.

A.q: Which organisation in an integrated care system plans NHS services for its population and manages the NHS budget?
A.why: Each ICS has one integrated care board, an NHS organisation responsible for planning health services for its population and managing the NHS budget (NHS England).

whyNot.0: The ICP is a joint committee that develops the integrated care strategy.
whyNot.1: Local authorities are responsible for social care and public health.
whyNot.2: Provider collaboratives are partnerships of trusts that deliver and transform services.

A.q: Mrs Hale coughs after drinks since her stroke. Which professional should assess her swallowing?
A.why: Speech and language therapists assess and manage swallowing difficulties (dysphagia) and advise on safe textures. Knowing team roles supports timely referral (P5.4; Code 13.2).

whyNot.0: Dietitians plan nutrition but do not assess the swallow itself.
whyNot.1: Occupational therapists focus on daily living skills and equipment.
whyNot.3: Physiotherapists focus on mobility and chest care.

A.q: What is the main role of an integrated care partnership (ICP)?
options: Employing all of the area's community nurses
A.why: The ICP is a joint committee of the NHS organisations and upper-tier local authorities in an ICS, with wider partners. It must develop a long-term strategy to improve health, care and wellbeing (NHS England).

whyNot.0: Managing the NHS budget is the ICB's role.
whyNot.2: Inspection is the role of regulators such as the CQC in England.
whyNot.3: Community nurses are employed by provider organisations, not the ICP.

B.q: Mr Ahmed, 80, has fallen twice at home. The team wants an assessment of hazards in his home. Who is best placed to do this?
options: A district nurse on a visit
B.why: NICE NG249 (2025) recommends a home hazard assessment, ideally by an occupational therapist, as part of falls prevention.

whyNot.1: Physiotherapists lead exercise and mobility work rather than home hazard assessment.
whyNot.2: Social workers assess care and support needs, not environmental hazards.
whyNot.3: District nurses may notice hazards, but NG249 names occupational therapists.

B.q: Within an integrated care system, which body is responsible for adult social care?
B.why: Upper-tier local authorities are responsible for social care and public health in their ICS area (NHS England, What is integrated care?).

whyNot.0: The ICB plans NHS services, not social care.
whyNot.1: Hospital trusts provide NHS care, not statutory social care.
whyNot.3: GP practices provide primary care, not social care.

B.q: Which of these is one of the four stated aims of integrated care systems?
options: Reducing the number of NHS trusts
Tackling inequalities in outcomes and access
Moving all care out of hospitals
Replacing the local councils' social care role
B.why: ICS aims: improve outcomes in population health and healthcare; tackle inequalities in outcomes, experience and access; enhance productivity and value for money; help the NHS support broader social and economic development (NHS England).

whyNot.0: Reducing trusts is not a stated aim of ICSs.
whyNot.2: Care is joined up across settings, not moved entirely out of hospital.
whyNot.3: Local authorities keep their social care responsibilities within the ICS.

C.q: Mr Doyle, 58, has COPD, drinks heavily and is sofa-surfing. He is medically fit for discharge. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Discharge him with a leaflet listing local support services
Keep him in hospital until he finds housing
Refer him to his GP to organise everything
With consent, involve housing, alcohol and other teams
C.why: Interagency working means involving partner agencies early so a person with complex needs leaves hospital with coordinated support (P7.1, P7.5), sharing information with his agreement (Caldicott 7; Code 5).

whyNot.0: A leaflet leaves a person with complex needs without coordinated support.
whyNot.1: Keeping a medically fit person in hospital is not appropriate and does not solve the problem.
whyNot.2: The GP is one partner; coordination should start before he leaves.

C.q: A care home nurse notices that a resident's discharge letter lists different medicines from those in the bag sent from hospital. What should she do?
options: Contact the hospital or GP to reconcile them; report it
Give the medicines in the bag, as they were dispensed
Give the medicines listed on the letter instead
Withhold all of the medicines until the GP visits next week
C.why: Transitions are a common point of medicines error. Discrepancies are resolved by reconciliation with the prescriber, and the gap is reported for learning (P7.6; NICE NG5; Code 18).

whyNot.1: Giving medicines without resolving a discrepancy risks harm.
whyNot.2: Choosing one source without checking may also be wrong.
whyNot.3: Withholding all medicines for a week risks serious harm.

C.q: A community team wants to know how well it supports people with several long-term conditions as they move between services. Which approach best reflects proficiency P7.7?
options: Ask people and families about the whole journey
Count the number of referrals the team makes each month
Audit how quickly letters are typed and sent
Ask staff which services they think work best
C.why: P7.7 asks nurses to monitor and evaluate the quality of people's experience of complex care. Asking people and families about the whole journey, including transitions, gives the most direct evidence (P6.9).

whyNot.1: Referral counts show activity, not people's experience.
whyNot.2: Letter turnaround is one process measure, not the overall experience.
whyNot.3: Staff views are useful but do not capture people's experience.

reteach.title: One orchestra, many instruments
reteach.question: Why does a complex piece of music need a score that every player follows?

blocks.body: Each professional and agency is an instrument: the speech and language therapist, the pharmacist, the housing team, the council's social workers. The ICB and ICP write the overall score for the area (plans, budgets, strategy). On the ward, the shared care plan and a named coordinator keep everyone in time, and the nurse often notices first when someone is out of tune.

blocks.h: Joining up care for one person

blocks.text: Board (ICB) = NHS planning and money. Partnership (ICP) = joint strategy with councils and others.

explain.body: 36 integrated care systems cover England, legally established on 1 July 2022 by the Health and Care Act 2022. Each brings together the NHS, upper-tier councils, the voluntary sector and other partners.

test.q: When were integrated care systems legally established across England?
test.why: ICSs were legally established on 1 July 2022, covering all of England (NHS England; Health and Care Act 2022).

whyNot.0: April 2013 was an earlier NHS reorganisation, not ICS establishment.
whyNot.2: April 2019 predates the Health and Care Act 2022.
whyNot.3: 30 June 2024 is when the NRLS was decommissioned.

explain.body: The ICB is the NHS body that plans services and manages the NHS budget, agreeing a joint five-year plan with providers. The ICP is a joint committee that writes the integrated care strategy.

test.q: Which body agrees a joint five-year plan with local NHS providers?
test.why: ICBs manage the NHS budget and work with providers to agree a joint five-year plan setting out the NHS contribution to the ICP's strategy (NHS England).

whyNot.0: The ICP produces the integrated care strategy rather than the NHS five-year plan.
whyNot.2: Local authorities must have regard to the strategy but do not agree the NHS plan.
whyNot.3: The CQC regulates providers; it does not plan services.

explain.body: SLT: swallowing and communication. OT: daily living, equipment, home hazards. Physio: mobility and chest. Dietitian: nutrition. Pharmacist: medicines review and reconciliation. Social worker: Care Act assessment and safeguarding.

test.q: Which professional is best placed to carry out a structured review of a person's many medicines before discharge?
test.why: Pharmacists carry out medicines review and reconciliation, which reduces errors at transitions (NICE NG5; P5.4).

whyNot.0: Dietitians advise on nutrition, not medicines review.
whyNot.2: Social workers assess care and support needs.
whyNot.3: Physiotherapists address mobility and chest care.

explain.body: Caldicott principle 7: the duty to share information for individual care is as important as the duty to protect confidentiality. Share what is needed, with the right people, explaining to the person.

test.q: Which Caldicott principle states that the duty to share information for individual care is as important as the duty to protect confidentiality?
test.why: Caldicott principle 7: the duty to share information for individual care is as important as the duty to protect patient confidentiality (National Data Guardian, 2020).

whyNot.0: Principle 1 is to justify the purpose for using information.
whyNot.1: Principle 3 is to use the minimum necessary information.
whyNot.3: Principle 8 is to inform patients and service users how their information is used.
